title: Quote Special Form and List Primitives: Code as Data
description: Adds quote special form (returns operand unevaluated) and list primitives: car (first), cdr (rest), cons (prepend), null? (empty check). Lists are nested Python lists. quote prevents evaluation: (quote (1 2 3)) returns a list, not a call. Test: nums=(quote (1 2 3)); car->1; cdr->[2,3]; cons 0 nums prepends 0; null? (quote ())->True; (quote (+ 1 2))->['+',1,2] (code as data).
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: tokenize and read unchanged: parses S-expressions to nested lists.
PRIMITIVES adds list ops: car (p[0]), cdr (p[1:]), cons ([a]+p), null? (p==[]). symbols starts with these.

evaluate: int->itself; string->lookup; define->bind; NEW quote at 42-43: returns x[1] unevaluated (hands back the list as data). if at 44-46: evaluates test, picks one branch. General call at 47-48: evaluates all parts.
quote is a special form: returns its operand WITHOUT evaluating it. This lets lists be data, not code. (quote (1 2 3)) returns the quoted list. (quote (+ 1 2)) -> ['+', 1, 2].

steps.question: Why must quote be a special form instead of a primitive function?
steps.answer: If quote were a function, its argument would be evaluated before the call. (quote (1 2 3)) would try to evaluate (1 2 3) as a function call first. quote must receive the raw unevaluated list structure.

steps.description: run: tokenizes, reads/evaluates each form, prints non-None results.
Output: 1 (car nums); [2, 3] (cdr nums); [0, 1, 2, 3] (cons 0 nums); True (null? (quote ())); ['+', 1, 2] (quote (+ 1 2) - code as data).
